 1                         I.     WITNESS IDENTIFICATION

 2   Q.   Please state your name and business address.

 3   A.   My name is Ann E. Bulkley. My business address is One Beacon Street, Suite 2600,

 4        Boston, Massachusetts 02108. I am a Principal at The Brattle Group (“Brattle”), a

 5        consulting firm that advises clients on regulatory finance and ratemaking issues.

 6   Q.   On whose behalf are you testifying in this proceeding?

 7   A.   I am filing testimony on behalf of Southwestern Public Service Company, a New

 8        Mexico corporation (“SPS”) and wholly-owned electric utility subsidiary of Xcel

 9        Energy Inc.

10   Q.   Are you the same Ann E. Bulkley who filed direct testimony on behalf of SPS

11        in this case?

12   A.   Yes.

 1                                          II.     PURPOSE

 2   Q.      What is the purpose of your Settlement Support Testimony?

 3   A.      The purpose of my testimony is to explain my support for the Comprehensive

4            Stipulation dated June 22, 2026 (the “Stipulation”) among SPS, New Mexico

5            Department of Justice, New Mexico Large Customer Group, Occidental Permian

6            Ltd., Louisiana Energy Services LLC, Federal Executive Agencies, Targa

7            Resources Corp., Walmart Inc., Coalition for Clean Affordable Energy, and

8            Prosperity Works (collectively, the “Signatories”). In particular, my testimony

 9           addresses the Stipulation’s treatment of SPS’s return on equity (“ROE”). 1

10   Q.      Are you sponsoring any attachments in conjunction with your Settlement

11           Support testimony?

12   A.      No, I am not.




              1
                New Mexico Public Regulation Commission, Case No. 25-00079-UT, Comprehensive Stipulation,
     June 22, 2026, at 3. I refer to the 9.50% ROE as the “Stipulated ROE”.

 1                                     III.     STIPULATED ROE

 2   Q.   Have you reviewed the terms of the Stipulation as it pertains to SPS’s ROE

 3        and overall rate of return?

 4   A.   Yes, I have. My understanding is that the Signatories have agreed to an ROE of

 5        9.50 percent and an overall rate of return of 7.59 percent to be used for calculation

 6        of the revenue requirement.

 7   Q.   Do you support SPS’s decision to agree to the Stipulated ROE?

 8   A.   Yes, I do. While the Stipulated ROE of 9.50 percent is below the low-end of my

 9        recommended ROE range for SPS of 10.25 percent to 11.25 percent, 2 I understand

10        that any stipulation represents the give-and-take among negotiating parties

11        regarding multiple, complex issues. In agreeing to these terms, the Signatories

12        agree that the interests of customers are served by the integrated result of the

13        Stipulation, including the ROE, capital structure and overall rate of return

14        provisions. It is my understanding that the Stipulation represents a reasonable

15        resolution of the disputed claims between the Signatories. Further, as discussed by

16        SPS witness Todd, A. Wehner, I understand SPS has determined that the terms of



          2
              Bulkley Direct, at 12.

                                                    3
                                       Case No. 25-00079-UT

                                                of
                                          Ann E. Bulkley

 1          the Stipulation would likely be viewed by the rating agencies as constructive and

 2          equitable in the current regulatory environment. 3 Therefore, in the context of the

 3          overall settlement an ROE of 9.50 percent represents a reasonable compromise

 4          among the Signatories.

 5   Q.     How does the Stipulated ROE compare to the cost of equity results presented

 6          in your Direct Testimony?

 7   A.     Figure 1 presents the results of the cost of equity analyses conducted in my direct

 8          testimony based on market data through September 30, 2025. As I discuss in my

 9          direct testimony, based on the analytical results shown in Figure 1 as well as

10          considering current and prospective market conditions, I recommend an ROE range

11          of 10.25 percent to 11.25 percent. Therefore, it remains my position that if this were

12          a fully litigated proceeding that SPS’s ROE should fall within the range of 10.25

13          percent to 11.25 percent. However, as I noted above, the Stipulation including the

14          Stipulated ROE of 9.50 percent is the result of the give-and-take among negotiating

15          parties regarding multiple complex issues and that the Stipulation as a whole

16          represents a balanced resolution that benefits both the interests of shareholders and

1    Q.      Are authorized returns in other jurisdictions a relevant benchmark to

2            consider in evaluating the Stipulated ROE?

3    A.      Yes, they can be when the corresponding market conditions are considered. The

4            Hope and Bluefield cases establish that authorized ROEs must be comparable to

 5           other investments of commensurate risk. 5 Therefore, the regulatory decisions of

 6           other utility regulatory commissions provide a range of reasonableness and a

 7           benchmark that investors consider in assessing the authorized ROE of one utility

 8           against the returns available from other regulated utilities with comparable risk.

 9   Q.      Have you compared the Stipulated ROE to the recent authorized returns for

10           other vertically integrated electric utilities?

11   A.      Yes. I have analyzed the recently authorized returns for electric utilities and applied

12           the following screening criteria to establish returns for vertically integrated

13           companies in regulatory jurisdictions comparable to New Mexico:

14               •   I have excluded limited-issue rider cases because these cases address only
15                   a specific issue or issues, such as the construction of generation assets and
16                   the associated incremental risk, and not a utility’s entire operations.



             5
                Federal Power Commission v. Hope Natural Gas Co., 320 U.S. 591 (1944) (“Hope”); Bluefield
     Waterworks & Improvement Co., v. Public Service Commission of West Virginia, 262 U.S. 679 (1923)
     (“Bluefield”).

                                                      6
                                     Case No. 25-00079-UT
                                    Testimony in Support of
                                   Comprehensive Stipulation
                                              of
                                        Ann E. Bulkley

 1           •   I have excluded jurisdictions that set ROEs using a formula as opposed to
 2               following an approach that is similar to what the Commission has typically
 3               considered in setting the ROE.

 4           •   I have excluded returns authorized in Arizona because those determinations
 5               are based on fair value ratemaking adjustments. Therefore, the ROE that
 6               was established in the Arizona cases may have been set on a different basis.

 7           •   Lastly, I excluded authorized returns that reflect a utility-specific penalty
 8               because an authorized ROE that includes a penalty is not indicative of a
 9               market-derived cost of equity.

10   Q.   How did the Stipulated ROE compare to the recently authorized returns for

11        vertically integrated electric utilities in regulatory jurisdictions comparable to

12        New Mexico?

13   A.   Figure 2 shows the authorized returns for vertically-integrated electric utilities

14        across the U.S. from 2021 through 2025 that met the screening criteria outlined

15        above. The Stipulated ROE of 9.50 percent is between 12 and 36 basis points below

16        average annual authorized returns for vertically integrated electric utilities over this

17        period. Further, as shown in Figure 2, as interest rates have increased from 2021

18        through 2025, the average annual authorized returns for vertically integrated

19        electric utilities have also increased. As a result, the Stipulated ROE of 9.50 percent

20        is towards the low-end of the range of authorized returns for vertically integrated

21        electric utilities in 2025. Placing greater weight on the more recent authorized

                                                 7

1            returns given the change in market conditions, if this were a fully litigated

2            proceeding, it would be my position that the authorized return for SPS should

3            exceed the recent annual averages. However, the Stipulated ROE falls within the

4            range of recent authorized returns and is the result of the give-and-take among the

 5           Signatories regarding multiple, complex issues. On that basis, I conclude that the

 6           Stipulated ROE is one reasonable outcome as compared to recent authorized returns

 7           for vertically integrated electric utilities.
